10:48 Istg this happened to me and I was so confused. One night during a time I was trying to fix my sleep schedule and build habits I set alarm for 6:00 am. But my father took away my phone cuz I had been watching yt late at night prior to this and I was devastated ki "I'm trying to fix my habits and this is what you do?" but since I didn't have a choice I just kept repeating to myself "Let's wake up at 6. Please!! Wake up at 6." And even though I was damn sure I wasn't gonna wake because "how can I wake up without an alarm if I can't even wake with one??" the otherwise happened. I slept at 12pm something (which is still late for me because I was overthinking and annoyed) and woke up at 5:57 am on the clock, out of breath for some reason. And at first I thought I was late because obviously, I didnt have an alarm to wake me up but after I checked the time I was actually so impressed by the power of our brain. I was still not sure of this because I could've just woken up cuz of some noise or anything (I'm a light sleeper) so I decided to put this to test. The next day I slept thinking "I'm gonna wake up at 8 am" and I did!!! I woke up at 7:48 am ish and damn was I not impressed by the caliber of human brain. We truly seem to forget that their was a time when phones didn't exist and humans relied on circadian rhythm solely. If someone actually wishes to try this, my best advice would be TO NOT VIEW SCREEN BEFORE BEDTIME (atleast an hour). The reason being, it disrupts our natural circadian rhythm, signaling the brain into thinking its day time. This is truly all you need, believe me. The only other thing you need to do is say " Wake up at _ am" only once or twice, remembering it and just see the magic. Parents were right, it's the damn phone🤡

11:40 i was admitted in hospital at the last stage of dengue where my doctor told my parents that we cannot tell whether she will survive this night because I was spitting blood and my organs were internally bleeding, each one of them. The doctor however, spoke to me as if I was getting discharged tomorrow. Every day he used to say that your condition has improved and mostly tomorrow you will go back to home and I believed it And this kept on going for a whole month when I was in ICU. The Doctors team and medical interns used to visit me and they took my photos as case study of what happens in the last stage of Dengue and I was completely unaware about it. I came back from the hospital as if nothing happened to me and all my family was crying and three months later I was informed about my true condition and and I learnt a very valuable lesson of speaking and being positive about yourself in life !
